requirement_text: EU/non-EU determination and application-route split: "The definition of EU/Non-EU applicants is based on fee assessment criteria." Self-check questions given: "Were you born outside the EU/EEA? Have you, or your parents, lived outside the EU/EEA for 3 of the last 5 years? Are you a non-EU/EEA National? Have you previously attended a third-level institution (in Ireland or elsewhere)?" "If you are deemed to be a non-EU candidate for fees purposes, you should apply directly to UCD."

requirement_text: EU-fee-status applicants must use CAO, not direct application: "In all cases, UCD applicants who are granted EU fee status will only be admitted through the Central Applications Office (CAO) system. This is in line with CAO policies and procedures and the National University of Ireland (NUI) matriculation regulations." UK-citizenship carve-out: "Students with UK citizenship and who meet the residency requirement will continue to be assessed for EU fees in the normal manner and should apply via the Central Applications Office (CAO). All other prospective applicants with UK citizenship who are assessed for non-EU fees should apply direct to UCD."
source_authority_note: ucd.ie is the official domain of University College Dublin, a public university under the Universities Act 1997; domain is .ie, not .edu/.ac./.gov.
researcher_notes: Confirms the EU/non-EU application-route split at UCD specifically, and adds a UK-citizenship nuance (post-Brexit UK nationals can still qualify for EU fee status and the CAO route if they meet an Irish/EU residency test) not seen at the other three institutions researched tonight.

requirement_text: General non-EU/EEA IB requirement: "24 or more total points and the award of the IB Diploma." "Both Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation are acceptable for meeting the stated Math requirements... for programmes with a Higher Level Mathematics requirement, we strongly recommend Analysis and Approaches." English: "Language A: 3 at Higher Level or 4 at Standard Level. Language B or Ab Initio: 4 at Higher Level or 6 at Standard (4 at either level if presenting IB through English)."
